_note: 원문 유형은 문장 삽입. insert를 가장 강하게 구성하고, 유형마다 passage를 다르게 paraphrase 한다.

passage: Density counts how many people occupy a space; crowding names the feeling that the space is too small.
The two are usually linked, and high density often brings sensory overload and rising anxiety.
Yet some psychologists refuse to treat crowding as automatically harmful.
In their view it is a neutral force that magnifies whatever a person already feels.
A fan eager for a concert therefore enjoys the show more because the hall is packed.
Someone dreading the same evening finds the packed hall unbearable.
Groups behave the same way, so an angry crowd grows angrier as it tightens.
Parks and pedestrian streets, by lifting the prevailing mood, work in the opposite direction.
choices: why cities should limit the number of residents per district
how crowding amplifies whatever mood or behavior is already present
why concert halls are designed to hold as many people as possible
how sensory overload permanently damages urban residents' health
why psychologists disagree about how to measure population density
theme.explanation_ko: 밀집감이 이미 존재하는 기분·행동을 증폭시킨다는 내용. ②가 주제.
theme.distractor_ko: ①인구 제한, ③공연장 설계, ④영구적 건강 피해, ⑤측정 논쟁은 본문 초점이 아니다.

passage: We should stop assuming that a crowd is always a problem.
Density is a number; crowding is a feeling, and the two must not be confused.
High density can indeed bring overload, lost control, and anxiety.
But crowding is better understood as a neutral amplifier of existing moods.
A person eager for a concert enjoys it more when the hall fills up.
A person dreading an event suffers more for exactly the same reason.
Planners must therefore shape the mood before they worry about the numbers.
Parks and pedestrian areas in dense districts are the practical way to do it.
choices: 도시는 인구 밀도를 법으로 제한해야 한다.
밀집감은 언제나 스트레스를 유발하므로 피해야 한다.
공연은 관객 수를 줄여 진행하는 것이 바람직하다.
밀집감은 기분을 증폭하는 중립적 요인이므로 분위기 설계로 다뤄야 한다.
감각 과부하는 개인의 성격 문제이므로 환경과 무관하다.
claim.explanation_ko: 밀집감을 중립적 증폭기로 보고 공간·분위기 설계로 다루자는 주장. ④.
claim.distractor_ko: ①인구 제한, ②회피론, ③관객 축소, ⑤성격 문제론은 본문 주장이 아니다.

passage: Psychologists separate density, a count, from crowding, a feeling.
High density is usually what produces the feeling of crowding.
That feeling has long been tied to overload, lost control, and anxiety.
Some researchers, however, call crowding neutral rather than negative.
They argue that rising density simply strengthens the mood already present.
Anticipation becomes stronger pleasure; dread becomes stronger misery.
In a group, the dominant behavior is what gets magnified.
Well-designed public spaces can therefore raise the mood a crowd magnifies.
choices: 밀집감은 예외 없이 스트레스와 불안을 낳는다.
밀집감은 이미 존재하는 기분과 행동을 증폭시킨다.
도시의 밀도는 측정할 수 없는 심리적 개념이다.
공원은 도시의 인구 밀도를 실제로 낮춘다.
공격적 집단은 밀도와 무관하게 폭력적으로 변한다.
gist.explanation_ko: 밀집감이 기존의 기분·행동을 증폭시킨다는 것이 요지. ②.
gist.distractor_ko: ①예외 없는 부정, ③측정 불가론, ④밀도 감소, ⑤무관론은 본문과 어긋난다.

passage: Density is a measurement; crowding is what the body makes of it.
Usually a high count is needed before people feel hemmed in.
That feeling has been blamed for overload, lost control, and anxiety.
But a second view treats crowding as neither good nor bad in itself.
On this view, density simply turns up the volume on whatever is already playing.
Excitement grows louder; dread grows louder too.
A hostile crowd therefore turns violent as it packs together.
Parks and walkways set a friendlier tune for the crowd to amplify.
choices: Turning Up the Volume: What Crowds Do to Our Moods
Why Concerts Should Sell Fewer Tickets
The Anxiety Epidemic in Urban Life
How Parks Reduce a City's Population
title.explanation_ko: 군중이 기존의 기분을 '증폭한다(볼륨을 높인다)'는 내용을 압축한 ①이 제목.
title.distractor_ko: ②밀도 측정법, ③티켓 축소, ④불안 유행, ⑤인구 감소는 초점이 아니다.

passage: Density counts bodies; crowding measures the feeling of too little room.
The feeling has usually been described in negative terms alone.
Some psychologists, though, see crowding as neutral.
For them a crowd is an amplifier, not a source.
Whatever mood arrives at the door leaves the hall louder.
The eager concertgoer therefore enjoys the evening more.
The reluctant guest endures it less well than before.
The same rule governs groups, whether they are cheerful or hostile.
implication.underlined: a crowd is an amplifier, not a source
choices: crowds create emotions that individuals never had
crowds strengthen feelings that already exist rather than creating them
crowds always make noise louder than individuals do
crowds prevent people from expressing their true feelings
crowds replace personal moods with a single shared mood
implication.explanation_ko: '군중은 증폭기이지 발생원이 아니다'는 비유는 감정을 새로 만드는 것이 아니라 기존 감정을 강화한다는 뜻이다. ②.
implication.distractor_ko: ①감정 창출, ③소음(문자적), ④표현 억제, ⑤단일 기분 대체는 모두 다르다.

passage: Environmental psychologists make a distinction between density and crowding.
Usually, high density is needed for the phenomenon of crowding, which makes people to experience sensory overload.
However, some psychologists see crowding as neutral rather than invariably negative.
They believe that people's moods and behaviors intensify as density increases.
If an individual is looking forward to a concert, crowding enhances their enjoyment.
But if they are dreading an event, crowding makes the experience even worse.
Put into a community setting, crowding may accentuate the dominant behavior.
Creating positive social spaces may help to lift the general mood.
grammar._grammar_note: ② 'to experience' 가 비문법. 사역동사 make 는 목적격보어로 원형부정사를 취하므로 'experience' 가 옳다.
grammar.explanation_ko: 사역동사 make는 목적격보어로 동사원형을 취하므로 ②는 'experience'가 되어야 한다. ②가 정답.
grammar.distractor_ko: ① between A and B, ③ see A as B, ④ 과거분사 분사구문 Put into ~, ⑤ 동명사 주어 Creating은 모두 옳다.

passage: Density is a physical count, while crowding is the psychological feeling of too little space.
High density usually produces crowding, along with sensory overload and anxiety.
Some psychologists nevertheless regard crowding as neutral rather than always negative.
In their view, moods and behaviors intensify as density increases.
Someone eager for a concert therefore finds that crowding weakens their enjoyment.
Someone dreading an event finds the same crowding unbearable.
In a group, crowding accentuates the dominant behavior.
Parks and pedestrian areas can lift the general mood and defuse tension.
vocab._vocab_note: ④ 'weakens' 가 의도적 오답. 증폭 원리에 따르면 기대하던 사람의 즐거움은 '높아지므로(enhances)' 'weakens'는 정반대이다.
vocab.explanation_ko: 밀집감은 기존 기분을 증폭하므로 기대하던 사람의 즐거움은 커진다. ④는 enhances가 되어야 하며 weakens는 정반대이다. ④가 정답.
vocab.distractor_ko: ①심리적인 ②중립적인 ③증폭되다 ⑤완화하다는 문맥상 모두 적절하다.

passage: Density counts people; crowding describes how little room they feel they have.
The feeling has usually been linked to overload, lost control, and anxiety.
A second view, however, calls crowding neutral rather than harmful.
On that view crowding functions as __________ of the mood a person brings with them.
An eager concertgoer therefore enjoys the packed hall more than an empty one.
A reluctant visitor suffers in exactly the same conditions.
Groups follow the rule too, and a hostile crowd hardens as it tightens.
Good public spaces work by improving the mood that density will magnify.
blank.explanation_ko: 기대하는 사람은 더 즐겁고 두려워하는 사람은 더 괴로워지므로, 밀집감은 기존 기분의 '증폭기(amplifier)'이다. ②.
blank.distractor_ko: ①대체물, ③측정치, ④위장, ⑤장애물은 뒤따르는 두 사례(즐거움↑·괴로움↑)를 설명하지 못한다.

irrelevant.intro: Environmental psychologists distinguish density, a physical count, from crowding, the feeling of having too little space.
sentences: High density usually produces crowding along with overload and rising anxiety.
Some psychologists, however, treat crowding as neutral rather than always negative.
They argue that moods and behaviors simply intensify as density rises.
Modern elevators are tested to carry a fixed maximum weight before installation.
An eager concertgoer therefore enjoys a packed hall, while a reluctant one suffers in it.
irrelevant.explanation_ko: 글은 '밀도와 밀집감 구분 → 중립적 증폭 → 사례'의 흐름인데 ④ '엘리베이터 하중 시험'은 무관하다.
irrelevant.distractor_ko: ①②③⑤는 모두 밀집감의 증폭 효과라는 흐름에 연결된다.

order.given: Environmental psychologists distinguish density, the physical count of people in a space, from crowding, the psychological feeling of having too little room.

blocks.A: Some researchers, however, call crowding neutral rather than invariably negative, arguing that moods and behaviors simply intensify as density rises.
blocks.B: The same rule governs groups, so a hostile crowd hardens as it tightens, while parks and pedestrian areas can raise the mood that density will magnify.
blocks.C: Usually the feeling requires a high count, and it has long been blamed for sensory overload, lost control, and mounting anxiety.

order.explanation_ko: (C)가 주어진 글의 crowding을 'the feeling'으로 받아 통념을 설명하고, (A)의 however가 그것을 뒤집으며, (B)의 'The same rule'이 (A)의 증폭 원리를 받는다. (C)-(A)-(B).
order.distractor_ko: (A)의 however는 뒤집을 통념이 앞에 있어야 하고, (B)의 'The same rule'은 그 규칙이 먼저 제시되어야 성립한다.

insert.insert_sentence: So if an individual is eagerly awaiting a concert, the sense of crowding actually heightens their enjoyment of the show.

passage_marked.text: Environmental psychologists separate density, a physical count, from crowding, the feeling of having too little space.
Usually a high count is required before crowding appears, bringing sensory overload and rising anxiety with it.
Some researchers, however, call crowding neutral and argue that moods and behaviors intensify as density rises.
But if that same person is dreading the evening, the press of bodies makes the experience even harder to bear.
Groups follow the identical rule, and a hostile crowd hardens as the space around it shrinks.

insert.explanation_ko: 주어진 문장의 So는 ③ 앞의 '기분·행동이 증폭된다'는 원리를 받고, 뒤 문장의 'But if that same person'이 주어진 문장의 an individual과 짝을 이룬다. ③이 정답.
insert.distractor_ko: ③이 아니면 'that same person'이 가리킬 사람이 없고, So가 이어받을 증폭 원리도 앞에 놓이지 않는다.

passage: Density counts people; crowding is the feeling of too little space.
High density usually produces that feeling.
It has long been tied to overload, lost control, and anxiety.
Some psychologists nevertheless call crowding neutral.
They hold that density intensifies whatever mood is already there.
Eager concertgoers enjoy the packed hall more than they otherwise would.
Reluctant visitors find the same conditions worse than they otherwise would.
Groups magnify their dominant behavior in the very same way.
summary.summary_template: Rather than being always harmful, crowding acts as a __(A)__ force that __(B)__ the mood a person or group already has.
summary.explanation_ko: 밀집감은 (A)중립적인(neutral) 힘으로서 이미 있는 기분을 (B)강화한다(strengthens). ③.
summary.distractor_ko: (A)는 negative/positive가 아니라 neutral, (B)는 creates/removes가 아니라 strengthens여야 한다.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 밀집감은 그 공연에 대한 그들의 즐거움을 더 높여 준다.
writing.answer: The feeling of crowding enhances their enjoyment of the performance.
writing.explanation_ko: 주어의 핵은 The feeling(단수)이므로 동사는 enhances.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 공격적인 집단은 밀도가 높아짐에 따라 폭력적으로 변할 수 있다.
writing.answer: An aggressive group may turn violent as density rises.
writing.explanation_ko: turn + 형용사(violent), as절은 '~함에 따라'의 비례 의미.

writing.question: 다음 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 일부 심리학자들은 밀집감을 언제나 부정적인 것이 아니라 중립적인 것으로 본다.
conditions: see A as B 구문을 쓸 것
writing.answer: Some psychologists see crowding as neutral rather than invariably negative.
writing.explanation_ko: see A as B(A를 B로 여기다) + B rather than C(C가 아니라 B).

writing.question: 다음 글을 읽고, 흐름상 빈칸에 들어갈 한 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
writing.context: Building parks and pedestrian areas in dense cities may lift the general mood and ___________ tension.

writing.question: 다음 밑줄 친 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.
writing.en_prompt: Put into a community setting, crowding may accentuate the dominant behavior ― an aggressive group may turn violent as density rises.
writing.answer: 공동체 환경에 적용하면, 밀집감은 지배적인 행동을 두드러지게 할 수 있다 — 공격적인 집단은 밀도가 높아짐에 따라 폭력적으로 변할 수 있다.
writing.explanation_ko: Put into ~는 과거분사 분사구문, accentuate(두드러지게 하다), turn violent(폭력적으로 변하다).

writing.question: 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 한 단어를 각각 쓰시오.
writing.summary: Some psychologists regard crowding as (A)___________ rather than always negative, because moods and behaviors (B)___________ as density increases.
writing.explanation_ko: (A)는 본문의 neutral, (B)는 moods and behaviors intensify에서 가져온다.
